With a massive NFL event comes numerous NFL betting opportunities for online sports betting . Fernando Mendoza is the overwhelming favorite to be selected No. 1 overall by the Las Vegas Raiders, but there are plenty of other DraftKings NFL Draft props than simply who gets selected first. Betting apps have plenty of 2026 NFL Draft props on individual players, positions and teams for prop betting on the NFL Draft. SportsLine NFL expert R.J. White has locked in some of his best bets for the 2026 NFL Draft at DraftKings, including picking star running back Jeremiyah Love, from Notre Dame, to be one of the first four picks in the NFL Draft 2026. White has locked in his five favorite DraftKings NFL Draft prop picks ahead of the opening round on April 23rd. Check them out below. NFL Draft predictions to target Ravens draft offensive lineman first (+130) The offensive line was a major issue for Baltimore last year, and it hasn't gotten any better with Tyler Linderbaum leaving for Las Vegas. Whether it's moving up a bit for Francis Mauigoa or Spencer Fano, taking a plug-and-play interior lineman like Olaivavega Ioane, or even selecting Kadyn Proctor as the heir apparent at left tackle, the Ravens should be using a draft like this that isn't considered stacked with blue-chip talent to stock up on help to address their biggest weakness. We saw a little shift from our initial recommendation to play this at +140 last week, but I believe it should be even odds at least. Trade NFL Draft props at Kalshi. Check out our Kalshi promo code review to see their latest offers. Carnell Tate draft position: Under 7.5 (-105) The market appears to be predicting a little bit of a slide for Tate after the Ohio State receiver was once considered the clear option for the Browns at No. 6. While I believe Cleveland will go with an offensive lineman at that spot, I don't know that Tate gets by the Commanders at No. 7, particularly if Jeremiyah Love and Sonny Styles go off the board in the top five. Tate would be a great running mate and eventual replacement for Terry McLaurin, and receiver is a clear need for Washington. Getting the underdog side of this market while having the potential to hit with either the Browns or Commanders seems like good value. Rueben Bain drafted before Mansoor Delane (-120) This is a head-to-head matchup available at DraftKings that I could see shifting quickly. Teams don't seem to be too worried about Bain's arm length, and on ability alone he has an argument to be taken in the top five in the same tier as Arvell Reese and David Bailey. Delane is probably the best corner prospect in the draft, though a team comfortable with Jermod McCoy's medicals could prefer him, and there is good enough depth at corner that I don't see Delane as a potential trade-up target like Bain could be. Bain's window could legitimately start at No. 4 overall and I can't see him getting past No. 9, while Delane's window starts at No. 8 and probably goes down to No. 12, unless the Cowboys are one of those McCoy teams. That leaves a small margin for Delane to win this matchup. Check out our bet365 bonus code review right now and get their latest sign-up promo. NFL Draft longshot picks Seahawks draft running back first (+380) The defending Super Bowl champions lost their Super Bowl MVP, and White thinks they may turn to the NFL Draft to replace him. The Seahawks declined to franchise tag or re-sign Kenneth Walker III after he rushed for 135 yards in Seattle's 29-13 Super Bowl win over the Patriots. Whether it's with the final pick in the first round or by trading back, White expects Seattle to prioritize a replacement. "No. 32 might be a little high for Jadarian Price, but I think there's a good chance the Seahawks are taking him with their first pick in a different spot," White said. "Running back is their clearest need with Kenneth Walker gone and Zach Charbonnet injured, and we saw how big an impact the rushing attack had in the Super Bowl last year. Seattle has just four picks and will likely prioritize adding more on Draft Day, and those late first-round picks are key for those looking to trade up (maybe for Ty Simpson?) as they come with a fifth-year option. I see the Seahawks making a trade back, then selecting Price in Round 2." Claim the latest BetMGM bonus code. Check out our BetMGM bonus code review now and get it. Jacob Rodriguez drafted in Round 1 (+380) With this draft class being perceived as short on top-tier talent, there is the potential for the back half of the first round to look even more different from consensus mock drafts than recent years. I see logic in examining the Round 1 pick market as a result for longshots we can take a chance on, and Rodriguez fits the bill. He and CJ Allen play a non-premium position at off-ball linebacker but have high floors and reasons to believe each could land in Round 1, especially to teams looking for a piece to come in and make an immediate impact. Rodriguez won a lot of hardware for his collegiate performance in 2025, and in particular, I could see a number of teams in the back half of Round 1 having him higher on their boards than we expect. Lions draft safety first (+3000) Brad Holmes is a best-player-available type of drafter, and with offensive lineman a massive -380 favorite in this prop, I see potential to take a big swing on a lottery ticket play. Detroit's pick at No. 17 is in the perfect range to target an excellent safety class that includes Dillon Thieneman (often tied to the Vikings one pick later) or Emmanuel McNeil-Warren, and even though the Lions have one of the best safety pairings in the league when healthy, there are injury concerns around both Kerby Joseph, who reportedly has a serious knee injury that clouds his long-term outlook, and Brian Branch, who tore his Achilles late last season. Every draft has position-team pairings in Round 1 that look surprising on the surface, and this is one that makes some sense. Looking to add some juice to the 2026 NFL Draft? The point is to bet props where the price is in your favor often enough to matter across a season. What are NFL player props? An NFL player prop is a bet on how an individual player will perform in a game. Instead of betting on the winner, point spread, or total score, you're betting on a specific outcome or statistic for that player. Common NFL player props include: Passing yards, completions, attempts, and passing touchdowns (quarterbacks). Rushing yards and rushing attempts (running backs, quarterbacks, and other rushers). Receptions and receiving yards (wide receivers, tight ends, and running backs). Anytime, first, and multiple touchdown scorers (eligible offensive players and defenses/special teams). Most player props are offered as over/under bets. For example, a sportsbook might set a quarterback's passing yards at 245.5. You can bet the over if you think he'll finish with 246 or more, or the under if you think he'll finish with 245 or fewer. Touchdown scorer props work differently: you’re simply betting whether a player scores, with the odds reflecting the sportsbook's assessment of how likely that is. One thing that makes player props different from game bets is how much they depend on the game script. A team that falls behind by three scores is likely to throw more and run less, which can boost passing and receiving opportunities while cutting into rushing volume. That's why our projections account for the expected game script when estimating how a player is likely to perform. How Dimers finds the best NFL player props A prop is only worth betting if you have a number to compare the price against. Building that number is where most of the work happens. Market-specific model s: We model each of our prop markets separately, allowing the projections to account for the factors that matter most to each type of bet. Multiple models, combined : We use multiple models within each market and combine their predictions into a single projection. This helps produce a more robust estimate than relying on any one model alone. Player and game context : The projections consider player usage, recent and historical performance, injuries and availability, opponent strength, coaching tendencies, and the expected game environment. We also incorporate advanced metrics and play-by-play data. From projection to probability : We run simulations of the upcoming game to estimate how often a player finishes over or under the specific line being offered. That gives us the probability shown on the board. Probability meets price : We compare our projected probability with the probability implied by the sportsbook's odds. When our number is higher, the difference is the edge. Props that clear our value threshold make the board. Updated throughout the week : Projections change as player availability, team news, game conditions, and sportsbook prices change. Our board updates accordingly. Our NFL player props model is built to give you a consistent way to compare player projections with the prices available at sportsbooks. Rather than relying on a single prediction or a general opinion about a player, we use market-specific projections to identify where the numbers may offer value. The model covers 12 NFL player prop markets, with projections built around the factors that influence each market. Those projections are then compared with the actual lines and prices being offered, so the edge reflects a bet you can actually place. The numbers also aren't static. NFL player props can change quickly as injuries, inactives, lineup news, game conditions, and sportsbook prices move. Our projections and board are updated throughout the week to reflect those changes. No model gets individual player performances right every time. Player props are inherently high-variance bets, and even a strong projection can lose on any given play or game. The aim is not to predict every outcome correctly but to identify prices where the numbers are consistently in your favor over time. articles.text: Week 1 NFL Player Props: Best Prop Bets & Predictions Skip to content Purchase Watch & Listen Login Dashboard Betting Fantasy Analysis Props Stats Content Sportsbook Newsletter Betting Fantasy Analysis Props Stats Content Sportsbook Newsletter Betting Week 1 NFL Player Props: Best Prop Bets & Predictions By Josh Shepardson | 2026-09-13T09:01:27-04:00 Sep 13, 2026 | View Larger Image NFL Best Prop Bets: Week 1 Picks Christian Watson Over 55.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Juwan Johnson Over 41.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Chase Brown Over 23.5 Receiving Yards (-111) Sharp Betting Tools: NFL Props: Lines & Odds NFL Spreads, Totals, & Moneylines NFL Weather Forecast & Potential Impact NFL Implied Team Totals NFL Week 1 Best Prop Bet: Christian Watson Over 55.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Watson tore his ACL on January 5, 2025, in Week 18 of the 2024 season. He made his season debut last year on October 26, 2025, in Week 8. Remarkably, Watson didn't skip a beat. In fact, he played the best football of his career. The speedster can get off to a fast start this year, and the Packers might lean into the passing attack more while sorting through their backfield with Josh Jacobs on the Commissioner's Exempt List. The matchup against the Vikings could also prompt them to pass more. Per TruMedia, the Vikings were tied for 12th in expected points added (EPA) allowed per designed rush in 2025 and fifth in yards before contact allowed per rush attempt (1.05). Minnesota's coverage tendencies also boost Watson's receiving outlook. According to the Fantasy Points Data Suite 2.0, the Vikings were first in two-high coverage rate (69.0%) and first in blitz rate (44.7%) in 2025. Watson rattled off a 20% target rate per route and 2.42 yards per route run (Y/RR) on 119 routes against two-high coverage in 2025. Furthermore, he had a 26% target rate per route and 2.47 Y/RR on 77 routes against the blitz last season, reeling in 10 receptions on 20 targets for 190 receiving yards. Watson exceeded 55.5 receiving yards only five times in 11 games in 2025. That said, the Packers have thinned their wide receiving corps, and Watson should exceed last year's 68.6% route participation rate in a less crowded wideout room. On a more expansive route participation rate, with a possible uptick in the Packers' passing rate from last year's 24th ranking in pass rate over expected (-2.1% PROE) out of the gate, Watson should clear 55.5 receiving yards. NFL Week 1 Best Prop Bet: Juwan Johnson Over 41.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Kellen Moore brought his fast-paced brand of offense to the Saints last year. New Orleans played at the NFL's fastest pace in 2025, which is favorable for play volume. The Saints were only 19th in PROE (-0.6%), but their passing tendencies ratcheted up down the stretch. In the final four weeks of the regular season, New Orleans was tied for third in PROE (5.0%). They did play the Titans during those four weeks, and Tennessee's defense faced an NFL-high 6.4% PROE. However, the Saints also played the Panthers, Jets, and Falcons in that period, and they ranked 25th (-1.6%), 21st (-0.3%), and 20th (0.3%), respectively, in PROE faced in the 2025 regular season. The Saints had a banged-up backfield at that point, but Moore's willingness to cut Tyler Shough loose can also be viewed as bullish for his trust in the young quarterback. Speaking of Shough, Johnson excelled with the rookie quarterback. In 10 games that Shough played at least 20 snaps last season, Johnson recorded a 71.3% route participation rate, 16.2% target share, 20% target rate per route, 17.7% air yards share, 8.9-yard average depth of target (aDOT), 4.6 receptions per game, 57.4 receiving yards per game, and 1.97 Y/RR. The pass-catching tight end cleared 41.5 receiving yards in five of his last eight games last year. That includes the final three, when he ripped off 89, 95, and 61 receiving yards. Johnson can pick up where he left off for the Saints, and with New Orleans serving as one of the week's biggest underdogs, he should be in a negative gamescript, necessitating the Saints air it out to keep up with Detroit's high-powered offense. NFL Week 1 Best Prop Bet: Chase Brown Over 23.5 Receiving Yards (-111) I'm not on an island on the Sharp Football Analysis team for this pick. Rich Hribar shouted out Brown over 23.5 receiving yards on the NFL Week 1 Best Bets & Player Props Show . A top-down view is immediately favorable for Brown's receiving outlook. Since 2023, the Bengals are tied for first in PROE (7.9%). Conversely, the Buccaneers have been the NFL's biggest pass funnel since 2023, facing the highest PROE (4.3%). The Bengals don't need their arm twisted to let Joe Burrow cook, but the matchup should also push them in that direction. The matchup is also tasty for Brown. In the 2025 regular season, the Bucs allowed the most receiving yards per game (50.1) and the most yards per target (9.90) to running backs. Brown should also be leaned on as an outlet against Todd Bowles ‘ blitz-heavy tendencies. Tampa Bay had the third-highest blitz rate (35.3%) in 2025, and they've had the second-highest blitz rate (40.8%) since 2023. Meanwhile, among players on the Bengals with at least 40 routes against the blitz since 2024, Brown is tied for second in targets per route run (0.25) and has 30 targets, 23 receptions, 158 receiving yards, and 1.30 Y/RR on 122 routes against the blitz. Finally, in 23 games in which Burrow has played at least 20 snaps since 2024, Brown has tallied a 48.0% route participation rate, 11.3% target share, 0.21 TPRR, 3.7 receptions per game, 23.8 receiving yards per game, and 1.20 Y/RR. Brown should surpass those marks against Tampa Bay's pass-funnel and blitz-heavy defense, putting him over 23.5 receiving yards. The draft is perhaps the biggest offseason event, with a new wave of talent entering the professional ranks, ready to leave their mark on the sport we all know and love. This year, we are not faced with any uncertainty regarding the number one overall as Fernando Mendoza is set to head to Las Vegas as the new franchise cornerstone. After Mendoza, there is a lot of uncertainty as to how the rest of the first round unfolds. With that, let’s dive into the top prop bets available for the upcoming first round. Doc’s Sports offers NFL expert picks for every game on our NFL predictions page. Top 5 Pick: Sonny Styles Perhaps the most intriguing prop bet is whether or not Sonny Styles will be drafted inside the Top Five. My answer is yes. We know that Mendoza will go first overall, followed by either David Bailey or Arvell Reese. Whichever of the two isn’t drafted second, will almost certainly be taken third. That leaves the fourth and fifth selections by the Tennessee Titans and New York Giants. Both need help on defense; however, both would love to draft Jeremiyah Love. That said, the other will jump at the chance of drafting Styles. It is also quite possible that a team like the Dallas Cowboys make a big move to jump into the Top Five and draft Styles. It is highly unlikely he will fall outside the Top Five. My Pick: Yes, -110 First Wide Receiver Drafted The wide receiver class is deep, with Day 2 selections offering incredible value for teams who wait to jump at the position. Makai Lemon, Jordyn Tyson, and Carnell Tate are widely regarded as the best three wide receivers in this class. While all three will likely be taken inside the Top 15, Tate will be the first receiver off the board for this class. Tate reeled in 51 catches for 875 yards and nine touchdowns in his last season at Ohio State. While Lemon is a strong option in the slot, and Tyson is going to be an enticing red-zone threat, Tate is the most well-rounded receiver. Do not expect Tate to slide out of the Top 10. My Pick: Carnell Tate -175 First Offensive Lineman Drafted This is another position group argument. There are four solid options to be the first offensive lineman off the board. The top-rated prospect according to most Big Boards is Francis Mauigoa out of Miami. Despite being one of the highest graded prospects, not only at the position, but in the entire draft, Olaivavega Ioane, Spencer Fano, and Kadyn Proctor all have potential to be the first offensive lineman drafted. Fano separates himself with his versatility. He can play on either side of the line, and he is arguably the most athletic of the aforementioned quartet. He is going to be a solid run-blocker and be cornerstone on the line. Mauigoa may slip in the draft due to recent injury concerns impeding on his availability as camps get underway and preparation for the season ramps up. My Pick: Spencer Fano +110 Position of 1st Player Drafted – Los Angeles Rams Shifting gears to another interesting prop bet is what position will a certain team draft first. Here, the Los Angeles Rams are almost certainly going to add an offensive weapon to keep their winning window open another year with Matthew Stafford’s future getting murkier and murkier. They are going to draft a wide receiver to run opposite Puka Nacua which could not only open the field up for their WR1, but it will also benefit the run game. Lemon has been connected to the Rams at pick 13. While the Rams lack draft capital and can be inclined to move back for more Day 2 picks, they are likely going to draft another young offensive talent with a lot of potential that can not only have an impact now, but also for their next quarterback in the years to come. My Pick: Wide Receiver -110 Team to Draft Kenyon Sadiq There is no question that Kenyon Sadiq is the best tight end in the class. He showcases similar physical characteristics as George Kittle, and he looks like he could be one of the next great tight ends. He hauled eight touchdowns last season at Oregon, and he recorded a 4.40 time for the Combines 40-yard draft. His athleticism pushes the ceiling higher for him to develop as a reliable blocker, but there is no question he will have an immediate impact, like that of Tyler Warren, in his rookie season. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers will be the beneficiaries of Sadiq’s athleticism. Tampa Bay lost the ever-reliable Mike Evans, and they will need to replace him with another solid target. That will be Sadiq, and there is a lot of value with +500 odds. My Pick: Tampa Bay Buccaneers +500 Team to Draft Ty Simpson Surely the Jets won’t mess this up. They will have the opportunity to take a generational talent with the second pick in the first round, but that won’t be a quarterback. Their quarterback situation is atrocious, with no long-term option in-house. With that, they will be aggressive in trading back into the first round in order to draft Ty Simpson. Their biggest competition will be the Arizona Cardinals (if they trade back) and the Pittsburgh Steelers who could be inclined to reach for Simpson’s services with the uncertainty around Aaron Rodgers. The Jets will have the first pick in the second round, and will be on the phones finding a suitor picking in the 20’s. There is great value here at +500 to bet on the Jets drafting a quarterback they really like. My Pick: New York Jets +500 7th Overall Pick The Washington Commanders will have the seventh selection in the first round barring any trades. A match made in heaven would be Tate being selected here. He is the most explosive receiver in this draft class and would be an incredible addition for Jayden Daniels. Washington’s offense took a huge step back in Daniels’ sophomore season, and adding Tate will turn that right around. They are very familiar with the quality of receivers that Ohio State puts into the NFL, as he would join Terry McLaurin if selected here. If Styles slips, look for him to be a possibility here, but he is going to be taken inside the Top Five. This will be one of the best selections of this year’s draft. CFL Best Bets for Week 17 Saskatchewan Roughriders vs. BC Lions Lions -3.5 (-120, FanDuel) BC has won six of its last seven games and enters this matchup rested after dismantling Montreal 48-29 in Week 15. The Lions lead the CFL with 429.7 net yards per game, while Nathan Rourke has topped 300 passing yards in his six appearances since returning from injury -- and in his last eight games overall. As if Rourke's strong run of play wasn't enough, Zander Horvath adds another dimension with 19 total touchdowns, including 16 on the ground, and he's the league's biggest threat near the goal line. Saskatchewan is getting healthier with A.J. Ouellette and Kian Schaffer-Baker returning, but the Riders scored only six points against Winnipeg in their last game and have dropped three straight on the road. BC also won the previous head-to-head meeting 30-16, and another victory would give the Lions the season-series tiebreaker in a crucial battle for second place in the West. Hamilton Tiger-Cats vs. Edmonton Elks Over 57.5 (-110, BetMGM) This is a high number, but both offenses have enough explosive potential to push the matchup beyond 57.5. Hamilton quarterback Harrison Frost is coming off career highs of 330 passing yards and three touchdowns, while Kurleigh Gittens Jr. has accumulated 166 receiving yards and three scores over his last two games. Betting on Frost to repeat that performance might be a stretch, but the Tiger-Cats need a bounce-back performance after dropping their last four games. Edmonton brings considerably more firepower on the other side. Cody Fajardo is on pace for the first 5,000-yard passing season of his career, Justin Rankin is approaching 1,000 rushing yards, and the Elks rank third in the CFL with 30.9 points scored per game. The Tiger-Cats are dead last with 23.4 ppg, but Hamilton's desperate playoff situation should also encourage an aggressive approach, particularly if Edmonton establishes an early lead at Commonwealth Stadium. Calgary Stampeders vs. Ottawa Redblacks Stampeders ML (-140, bet365) Last week's 40-38 thriller showed why laying points with Calgary carries some risk, but the moneyline offers a cleaner path against an Ottawa team that remains 0-13. Vernon Adams Jr. threw for 357 yards in that victory, while newcomer Deonta McMahon immediately strengthened Calgary's backfield with 102 rushing yards on 15 carries. Ottawa certainly looked more dangerous with McLeod Bethel-Thompson under center, as the veteran threw a career-high five touchdowns, but the Redblacks still couldn't finish the job despite producing their highest point total of the season. Calgary remains firmly involved in a crowded West playoff race, and at -140, backing the Stampeders to win is more appealing than asking them to cover another road spread, especially considering they'll be facing a winless team. Moore is coming off two lackluster seasons by his standards, but a new environment and the opportunity to play with Josh Allen may have created the perfect recipe for an excellent buy-low opportunity. Moore has been seen smiling throughout training camp as he enters 2026 in a dramatically different situation after being traded from Chicago to Buffalo. Instead of playing in an environment where something was clearly not right personally and in a Ben Johnson offense where his target share declined significantly, Moore now gets to catch passes from a former MVP quarterback while reuniting with Joe Brady , his former offensive coordinator in Carolina. The biggest reason to bet Moore’s over is simple: Allen is without a doubt the best quarterback Moore has ever had passing him the ball. Moore has spent most of his career dealing with inconsistent quarterback situations, yet he has still exceeded 1,000 receiving yards in four seasons. He enters his ninth season averaging more than 1,000 receiving yards per season. Moore is also a huge upgrade at the wide receiver position for Allen. The Bills have not produced a 1,000-yard-wide receiver in either of the previous two seasons since Stefon Diggs ’ departure, while their average target depth ranked last in the NFL in 2025. Moore doesn't need an unreasonable target share to beat his season-long receiving-yardage line, but he should command a target share over 20% given the receiver depth in Buffalo. The Bills entered the 2024 season with a new slogan: Everybody Eats. Sean McDermott tried to spin that into a positive after the Bills parted ways with Diggs. However, targets are earned. The “Everybody Eats” slogan was admitting to everyone what was glaringly obvious: There wasn’t an alpha target earner on the roster. In an interview, Ian Rapoport talked about Moore as a breakout candidate for the upcoming fantasy season, but fantasy gamers should be aware that “the Buffalo Bills like to spread the ball around.” Again, this is a mythical statement and is a byproduct of a lackluster receiving room. Diggs was a member of the Buffalo Bills from 2020 to 2023. In those four years, he led all NFL receivers in receptions, was second in targets, and had 28.0% of the Bills' total team targets over that span. Before last season, Moore had four consecutive seasons in which he had over 26% of his team’s targets. In 2021, Brady’s final season as the Carolina Panthers offensive coordinator, Moore had 28.3% of the team's targets and 40.2% of the team’s total air yards. In that season, Moore caught passes from Cam Newton , Sam Darnold , and PJ Walker and still exceeded 1,150 receiving yards. The projections in the Sharp Football Analysis Draft Kit are bullish on Moore joining the Bills. Our projections have Moore projected for 83 receptions and more than 1,100 receiving yards, well over the season-long yardage prop. One of the biggest risks of betting season-long overs is injury. Moore has played every game in the past five seasons and has played 15 or more games in all eight seasons to start his career. Moore has played through injury in the past, which helps give him the opportunity to continue to accumulate volume over the full season. The market may be overreacting to Moore’s 2025 season and overconfident that his decline is age-related. In addition to our projections supporting the over, in the Wide Receiver Trends article, Rich Hribar highlighted that when searching for wide receivers to exceed expectations, one of the more common hits comes from players changing situations, making Moore a solid bet this season. sophomore NFL season as a breakout candidate. Loveland was selected in the top 10 of the 2025 NFL Draft and entered the league with an elite tight end profile and skill set. Loveland started his rookie season slowly as he missed part of training camp with an injury and played a part-time role in the Bears offense in the opening months of the season. He opened his rookie season with just 5 receptions and 54 yards in the opening five games while he was still establishing himself within Ben Johnson ‘s offense and managing an injury. Loveland’s role and production accelerated dramatically as the season progressed. He finished the regular season and playoffs with four consecutive double-digit target games, including a 15-target game in the Bears' playoff victory against the Packers. The late-season production provides a much better indication of what Loveland could look like with a full-time role throughout the entire season. Loveland shared the field with rookie wide receiver Luther Burden for 173 passing plays and generated more targets, air yards, and receiving yards than the hyped second-year receiver. Both Loveland and Burden are projected for increasing roles in Year 2. However, Loveland may still be overlooked. Loveland led the Bears in receiving yards despite only being on the field for 63.8% of the team's dropbacks. With the Bears trading D.J. Moore and not investing much capital into a replacement, there is a significant opportunity for Loveland to increase his target share in an ascending offense. In the final five weeks of the regular season, the Bears had multiple tight ends on the field on 56.9% of the offensive plays. The increase of 13 personnel benefited Loveland the most as he averaged 3.34 yards per route and had 32.4% of the team's targets with three tight ends on the field. Johnson recently did an interview in which he stated that he wants the 2026 Bears to be the highest-scoring offense ever . The Bears have the seventh-most difficult strength of schedule in 2026, after the ninth-easiest last season. Injuries to Coby Bryant and Kyler Gordon are concerning for a defense which is not particularly deep with talent in the secondary, which could force the Bears into more shootouts, boosting Loveland’s ceiling. The Sharp Football Analysis projections have Loveland projected for 90 receptions and 1,068 receiving yards, which is not unreasonable given his late-season production. In the final game of the regular season and two playoff games, Loveland was targeted on 43.3%, 31.3%, and 37.0% of his routes. That is unsustainable, but it indicates that Loveland can push for a 22-25% target share through an entire season. Including the playoffs, Loveland averaged 9.9 air yards per target, which led all tight ends in the league, and gained 20 or more yards on 21.4% of his receptions. The ability to operate deeper down the field and create explosives means that a relatively modest increase in targets can produce substantial increases in yardage. Another important component in Loveland’s ascent is Caleb Williams . Williams registered an off-target throw on 15.9% of his passes targeted at the rookie tight end last season. Entering his third season in the NFL and second season with Johnson, Williams appears more comfortable running the offense than a year ago. Even a slight improvement in accuracy benefits Loveland. Given the way his role expanded throughout 2025, the 2026 season could be the year Loveland goes from promising rookie to legitimate NFL receiving weapon who is mentioned in the same sentence as Brock Bowers and Trey McBride when discussing the league’s high-upside tight ends.
